top_story_title: Cisco patches authentication-bypass flaws in Identity Services Engine and ISE-PIC
top_story_summary: Cisco has published an advisory covering multiple vulnerabilities in Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and the Cisco ISE Passive Identity Connector (ISE-PIC). Cisco states that a remote attacker could use them to access or manipulate data, obtain sensitive information, or cause a reload of certificate and key material on an affected device. Software updates are available and Cisco states there are no workarounds.
top_actions: Inventory every ISE and ISE-PIC node, including secondary PAN, MnT and PSN roles, and record the exact running version and patch level of each.

Open the Cisco advisory (cisco-sa-ise-multiauth-bypass-sgD2HbL4) and check the running versions against its fixed-release table - no fixed version is stated in the feed item, and Cisco states there are no workarounds.
Schedule the upgrade across the deployment in Cisco's documented node order rather than node-by-node ad hoc; validate persona replication and certificate services after each step.
Confirm the ISE admin and API interfaces are reachable only from the management network, and that no ISE node answers on an internet-facing or user VLAN.
Review the other advisories in the September 16, 2026 Advance Notification group - this one is not standalone, and a single change window should cover the set.
executive_summary: One network-device item in this 24-hour window: Cisco's advisory for multiple authentication-bypass vulnerabilities in Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE Passive Identity Connector (ISE-PIC). Software updates are out; Cisco states there are no workarounds.

No CVE IDs, affected versions or fixed releases appear in the collected advisory text, and nothing in this window is on the CISA KEV catalog. Read the fixed-release table in the Cisco advisory before scheduling anything.
The ISE advisory belongs to a group published under Cisco's Advance Notification for Publication of September 16, 2026 - plan one change window for the set rather than treating this as a single fix.

The two other items collected were Check Point AI-security blog posts about prompt injection against a typed decision model and about governing enterprise AI agents. Neither concerns network infrastructure devices, so both are dropped from the digest.
Quiet window, thin sources: 709 raw items, 56 in window, 4 on topic. Absence of news here is not evidence that your fleet is current.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Identify all ISE and ISE-PIC nodes from the asset inventory, by persona (PAN, MnT, PSN, pxGrid) and running version and patch level.

**Cisco** — Check each running version against the fixed-release table in Cisco advisory cisco-sa-ise-multiauth-bypass-sgD2HbL4 and schedule the upgrade in a change window; Cisco offers no workaround, so mitigation alone does not close this.

headlines.title: Cisco Identity Services Engine Authentication Bypass Vulnerabilities
headlines.summary: Cisco patched multiple authentication-bypass flaws in Identity Services Engine and ISE-PIC that let a remote attacker read or alter data, or reload certificate and key material.
